- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.6), model underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast with no recent sentiment support, reduce peak by 5–10% and add a 1–2 day lag in the spike’s timing.  
- If model consistently underestimates in the 10–15 day horizon, apply a 3–5% upward bias to forecast for that window.  
- If model overestimates in the 20–30 day horizon, apply a 3–7% downward bias, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day windows; if forecast is > 2σ above recent mean, reduce by 1–3σ.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), model tends to lag; add 1–2 day delay to forecast adjustments.
